title: Affine finite-projective-space presentations of finite-type projective bundles
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal E$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. There exist an affine open covering $S=\bigcup_{\alpha\in I}U_\alpha$, integers $n_\alpha\geq0$, and sections $s_{\alpha,0},\ldots,s_{\alpha,n_\alpha}\in\Gamma(U_\alpha,\mathcal E|_{U_\alpha})$ generating $\mathcal E|_{U_\alpha}$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections], with the following property. The restriction $\mathcal E|_{U_\alpha}$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type, and there is a closed immersion of $U_\alpha$-schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]
$$j_\alpha:\mathbf P_{U_\alpha}(\mathcal E|_{U_\alpha})\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{n_\alpha}_{U_\alpha}.$$
Here the source is $\operatorname{Proj}_{U_\alpha}(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_{U_\alpha}}(\mathcal E|_{U_\alpha}))$, with projective bundle and symmetric algebra as in [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], and the target and its structural map are the finite projective space of [def-kun-projective]. The projection of the source to $U_\alpha$ equals the projective-space projection composed with $j_\alpha$; in particular it is H-projective in that convention. No finite bound on $I$ or uniform bound on the integers $n_\alpha$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 01WB (lemma-characterize-locally-projective), proof choosing affine neighbourhoods and finite generators; Tag 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), proof paragraph beginning If E is generated by finitely many global sections; Modules Tags 01B5 (definition-finite-type) and 01AM (definition-globally-generated).

proof.text: Finite type supplies local finite generating families. Around each point choose an affine open inside one of their domains using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Restrict the family through the over-category restriction functor and the equivalence with modules on the open subscheme. These functors preserve the free module and epimorphic evaluation, so the resulting family still generates. Reindex a finite family by Fin(card I), and append a zero section to obtain Fin(card I+1), including when I is empty. The old evaluation factors through the new one, so the new evaluation is epic. A finite generating family gives finite type via its local-generators data. Indexing these choices by points gives an affine open covering, also for the empty scheme.

source.place: Tag 01WB (lemma-characterize-locally-projective), proof choosing affine neighbourhoods and finite generators; Tag 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), proof paragraph beginning If E is generated by finitely many global sections; Modules Tags 01B5 (definition-finite-type) and 01AM (definition-globally-generated).

proof.text: Restriction along an open immersion preserves quasi-coherence by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. For a quasi-coherent module E with finitely many global generators s_i, the free module on these generators is quasi-coherent by the proved source-library free-module instance (the identity presentation with zero relations). On an affine open V, [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] identifies the range of evaluation with the kernel of its cokernel map. Since evaluation is epic that cokernel map is zero, so evaluation on V is surjective. The finite biproduct identity, followed by evaluation, expresses each section as a linear combination of the restricted s_i.

source.place: Tag 01WB (lemma-characterize-locally-projective), proof choosing affine neighbourhoods and finite generators; Tag 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), proof paragraph beginning If E is generated by finitely many global sections; Modules Tags 01B5 (definition-finite-type) and 01AM (definition-globally-generated).

proof.text: For every affine V, define q_V from O(V)[T_0,...,T_n] to Sym(E(V)) by T_i mapping to the symmetric image of s_i restricted to V. This is an explicit polynomial evaluation homomorphism. It preserves homogeneous degree: the degree-one polynomial span maps into the symmetric degree-one range, and taking powers proves the assertion in every degree. It is surjective: span induction puts every symmetric generator in its range by the previous step, and symmetric-algebra induction handles scalars, sums and products. Polynomial extensionality proves naturality in V, since both maps restrict scalars and send each variable to the restriction of its chosen section. These are precisely the section rings, degrees and restriction maps of [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra].

source.place: Tag 01WB (lemma-characterize-locally-projective), proof choosing affine neighbourhoods and finite generators; Tag 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), proof paragraph beginning If E is generated by finitely many global sections; Modules Tags 01B5 (definition-finite-type) and 01AM (definition-globally-generated).

proof.text: Use the affinePolynomialEquiv of [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] to regard q_V as a homomorphism from the affine section algebra of relative projective space. The polynomial restriction equation in [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space] and the previous naturality calculation give a morphism of affine-basis graded algebras. It respects the structural algebra maps and is surjective on every affine section ring. By [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] its contravariant relative Proj map is a closed immersion, and the relative-Proj structural-map equation shows that it is over the base [def-nagata-relative-proj].

source.place: Tag 01WB (lemma-characterize-locally-projective), proof choosing affine neighbourhoods and finite generators; Tag 087S (lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective), proof paragraph beginning If E is generated by finitely many global sections; Modules Tags 01B5 (definition-finite-type) and 01AM (definition-globally-generated).

proof.text: Compose this immersion with the over-base isomorphism to base-change projective space from [lem-trf-free-projective-bundle-base-change-space]. Composition with an isomorphism preserves closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and the structural-map equations compose. The resulting factorization is H-projectivity [def-kun-projective]. Apply the construction independently to every chosen affine neighborhood; neither the covering nor the ranks require a finite uniform bound.

lean.statement: theorem exists_affine_projectiveBundle_presentations (S : Scheme.{u}) (E : S.Modules) (hE : E.IsQuasiCoherentFiniteType) : ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → S.Opens) (n : I → ℕ), (⨆ a : I, U a) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ a : I, IsAffineOpen (U a) ∧ ∃ s : ULift.{u} (Fin (n a + 1)) → (E.restrict (U a).ι).sections, Epi ((E.restrict (U a).ι).freeHomEquiv.symm s) ∧ ∃ hq : (E.restrict (U a).ι).IsQuasicoherent, (E.restrict (U a).ι).IsFiniteType ∧ ∃ j : (@SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData (U a).toScheme (E.restrict (U a).ι) hq).relProj ⟶ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (n a + 1)); (U a).toScheme), IsClosedImmersion j ∧ j ≫ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (n a + 1)); (U a).toScheme) ↘ (U a).toScheme = (@SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData (U a).toScheme (E.restrict (U a).ι) hq).relProjHom ∧ IsHProjective (@SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData (U a).toScheme (E.restrict (U a).ι) hq).relProjHom
